A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReStraV research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation-geometry analyses, ReStraV detection results in Tables 1–4 and Figure 7, and sampling and temporal-window ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds one-to-many detection, Veo3 evaluation, expanded encoder comparisons, permutation feature importance and scene-cut measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 embeddings, the same distance and curvature calculations, the 21-dimensional classifier input and the same classifier choices. Testing additional encoders and analyzing feature importance do not establish a change to the deployed method.

E1.justification: Section 7 adds the DeMamba one-to-many benchmark and Veo3 evaluation, extending coverage to previously untested sources such as SEINE, OpenSora, MorphStudio, HotShot, Show-1 and MoonValley. VidProM, GenVidBench, Physics-IQ and the existing natural-video coverage are retained.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares ReStraV with NPR, STIL, TALL and DeMamba in the one-to-many experiment; the earlier detector comparison sets remain. Figure 2B also expands the evaluated encoder alternatives from eight to fourteen, adding human-vision-inspired, spatiotemporal and adversarially trained models.

E3.justification: New protocols train separately on Pika, SEINE or OpenSora and evaluate across ten unseen sources, and test the existing MLP without Veo3 training on 200 Veo3 and 200 natural videos. Added analyses specify individual-feature shuffling and scene-cut measurement on 13,000 videos per class. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds permutation importance for all 21 features, a scene-cut confound analysis, and an expanded encoder study examining whether absolute straightening predicts discrimination. These substantially extend the questions investigated. The original video-length, sampling-density and temporal-window ablations are retained in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Section 4 adds a correlation analysis between absolute straightening and detection capability, reporting rho = -0.13 and p = 0.64. Existing t-tests, ANOVA and mean-plus-standard-deviation ablation reporting remain. No explicit increase in repeated runs or newly specified seed counts is documented.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds one-to-many results: ReStraV has the highest F1 in all three training settings, while DeMamba has higher AP throughout. The Veo3 test reports 83.2% accuracy, 85.1% F1 and 86.9% AUROC. Figure 2B revises some retained encoder gaps, alongside new encoder, feature-importance and scene-cut findings. Tables 1–4 and the Physics-IQ detection scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The displacement, Euclidean distance, angular curvature and aggregated-feature definitions remain mathematically unchanged. The distinction between absolute and differential straightening is developed conceptually and empirically; no new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and discussion summary retain the same central claims: efficient, geometry-based detection using pretrained representations, with strong performance across generators and encoders. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 now explicitly distinguishes absolute perceptual straightening from differential straightening of natural versus synthetic videos, arguing that the latter explains detection despite negative gaps in human-vision-inspired models. New interpretations identify aggregated features as dominant and discuss shot boundaries and scene-cut frequency as potential limitations or confounds.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and identifies PySceneDetect as the tool used for scene-cut analysis. Original preprocessing, classifier settings, hardware and timing disclosures are retained. Some comparative detail is lost: Figure 2B no longer labels the selected layer for each encoder. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new detectors, encoder families, generators and analyses, and expands AI-safety and privacy citations. Section 2 explicitly distinguishes synthetic-content detection from trajectory-based perceptual-quality assessment. These broaden the literature context without substantially replacing the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 4 is locally rewritten and reordered; related work and broader impacts are revised. Benchmark subsections become lettered paragraphs, and appendices are regrouped and relabeled A–E. Most introductory, methodological and existing experimental prose remains substantially intact, with additional caption and author-text edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and figures for feature importance, Veo3 examples and scene-cut frequency. Figure 2B is redesigned as a horizontal, model-family-colored comparison; other figures are resized or restyled. Tables and appendix figures are substantially rearranged, with new running headers and takeaway-box styling. Retained plots are distinguished from newly added displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and explanation through one-to-many comparisons with specialist detectors, an unseen Veo3 test, and analyses of encoder behavior, feature reliance and possible scene-cut confounding. These address important gaps in v1's support for generalization and its mechanistic explanation. New protocols remain briefly documented, some encoder-layer details disappear, and inherited inconsistencies such as the Plants average in Table 4 versus the prose persist. Nevertheless, the added targeted evidence and clearer distinction between absolute and differential straightening provide a substantial net quality gain.
